summary: Thomas Borchert is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who was a PhD candidate at the University of Chicago (attested 2005). He served as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Burrow was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Cambridge, SOAS, and Annamalai University under E. J. Rapson and P. S. Subrahmanya Sastri. He served as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1944 to 1976.

Thomas Christian Tychsen was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel University and the University of Göttingen, where he later held an academic post from approximately 1785 to 1834.

Thomas Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He earned a PhD from Harvard University, where he studied under E. Bruce Brooks, and a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.

Thomas Doctor is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and conducted doctoral research at the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, having also been supervised for his MA by Christian K. Wedemeyer.

Thomas E. Crow studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at CalArts, Chicago, Princeton, Michigan, Sussex, Yale, and USC, directed the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor of Modern Art at NYU in 2007.

Thomas E. Wood is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies who completed his BA and PhD at the University of California, Berkeley. He held posts at California State University, Fresno, and SUNY New Paltz.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke studied at Eton College and East India Company College, and under Jagannatha. Working in Indology and history, he served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who earned his PhD from Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman. He served as Executive Editor at Columbia University (attested 2007).
Thomas Henry Huxley studied at Great Ealing School, University College London, and Charing Cross Hospital Medical School. He held a post at Imperial College London from approximately 1854 to 1885.

Thomas James Mazanec is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Calvin University and earned an MA from the University of Colorado. His doctoral supervisors included Anna M. Shields and Stephen F. Teiser.

Thomas Jülch is a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Frankfurt, Hull, Heidelberg, and Munich (PhD c. 2006–2011). He worked as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University from 2013 to 2019.
Thomas Kintaert is a scholar in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies who held an attested post at the University of Vienna in 2009 and 2022.
Thomas M. Hunter is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He served as Dean at the University of Virginia and held an affiliation at the University of British Columbia (attested 2011).

Thomas Nathan Patton is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his PhD at Cornell University under Anne M. Blackburn. He held a post at the City University of Hong Kong (attested 2018).

Thomas Oberlies is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Albrecht Wezler and Paul Thieme. He held posts at the University of Tübingen (attested 1988), Zurich (1990), and Freiburg (attested 2001).

Thomas P. Kasulis is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He held a post at Ashland University (~1981–1991) and served as a professor at Ohio State University from approximately 1991 to 2014.

Thomas R. Trautmann is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He held posts at the University of Michigan, serving as co-director in 1980 and continuing with an attested affiliation in 1991.
Thomas Robert Malthus studied at Warrington Academy from around 1782 to 1784 before continuing his studies at Jesus College and the University of Cambridge from 1784 to approximately 1788.

Thomas Roebuck was a scholar of linguistics and Indology educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh. He was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1809–1819) and served as assistant-secretary and examiner at the College of Fort St George (1811).
